values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c95fdb62-b368-4b6: Ever wanted to start growing food, but don't know where to start? Emanuel J. Lacy will talk you through the basics of growing delicious herbs to add some spice to your cooking.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8cec4b46-86cb-470: Hey there, I'm Emanuel J. Lacy, and this is my garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_6e8c1320-73bf-440: Flowers, crops, and trees all beautiful to look at, perfectly balanced with nature.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_01e39ae4-f2e9-4af: But I didn't start out with a big dream.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e2ad820a-4d4f-4de: I started with some pots of parsley, and a dream.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_f6b4efe5-19d4-445: Herbs are the perfect place to start your gardening or farming life.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_dd324eb6-7319-435: Simple to grow, there's still some tricks that will help you get the best herbs.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8427a40e-8283-4ad: Each has a growing season, as you can see on-screen now.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1d456672-d367-4ef: Most herbs can be grown from seed, but it's best to grow from cuttings if you can.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c099c473-39b9-4a6: Start them in pots near the end of winter, then plant them outside.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_419de859-4db5-457: They all grow best in full sun, on well drained soil.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_0a27bc3b-3d93-49d: That's about it. You'll soon have some healthy herbs...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_05e3ca62-9b02-4ce: ... and be ready to move on to something more complex.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_68e705de-edd5-42a: VHS: Growing Fruit and Veg at Home 1
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d41d649a-605d-4b5: Growing Fruit and Veg at Home 1
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bedf9343-c13c-4a7: With even a small garden, you could slash your food bills - and eat a lot healthier - by growing some of your own food. With this helpful VHS guide, Emanuel J. Lacy will teach you how and when to grow carrots, broccoli, radish, and more!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_72dca849-1d5a-482: Hey there, I'm Emanuel J. Lacy, and this is my garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d25ca4ba-6a16-488: Ain't it pretty? But it's not just for looks I planted most of it.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_620a3d47-6f41-46b: There's some good eatin' there too.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_950630dc-9d14-482: It's best to start small and simple. Potatoes and cabbage are the easiest to start with...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_2cfa6574-608f-460: Potatoes are usually grown from seed potatoes, while cabbage is grown from seed.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_882a0767-b5a9-476: Then you'll be ready to try radishes, carrots, onions, and broccoli...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e9e0232e-4295-40c: Finally, strawberries are a little trickier, and tomatoes require staking...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_96394994-c069-43b: ... good for a higher level gardener.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1bf6624c-6776-482: Keep 'em watered, and examine them closely for diseases and pests.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_469fb867-d417-4c7: I will have another video coming out soon specifically about those...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_aa094061-c6a8-4b6: ... so keep an observant farmer's eye on your local store shelves!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ae21bcac-c36a-44c: Soon, you'll have a garden full of crops that are not just free...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bd2eb6d9-0367-47f: VHS: Growing Fruit and Veg at Home 2
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_f81b6664-c568-48f: Growing Fruit and Veg at Home 2
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_69809ace-98f9-40b: Emanuel J. Lacy returns to teach you how and when to grow even more food, including corn, kale, and sweet potatoes.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_6ae82413-3b91-45e: Hey there, I'm Emanuel J. Lacy, and this is my garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d680f58e-7937-411: In my previous video, I talked about some staple foods you can grow in your plot or garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_282d5377-28cc-42d: Now we'll talk about crops that are a little more complex, or exotic.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_de69c367-5771-44e: Green peas are easy to grow, but they need to climb or they can collapse and rot.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a3e9f132-dddb-4c0: Soybeans are self-supporting, and so a little easier to maintain.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_08a9c4ce-21b3-4bb: Kale is just cabbage with a college education, pretty easy to grow.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e93e8814-b1d0-466: Garlic is another favorite. Good for the blood, and keeping the vampires away.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_514852c0-0288-467: Sweet potatoes are great at surviving droughts.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_7ae0159e-b0d8-44d: Everybody knows how tall corn grows, so you'll need a big plot.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_841218a8-84db-4ab: Grow your corn away from anything you don't want it in the shade.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_08cb8449-f431-4a9: It grows slowly, but the yields are a-maize-ing! Hehe.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_32996011-3abf-4f9: VHS: Controlling Nasty Crop Pests and Diseases
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_306243ad-ba3e-48f: Controlling Nasty Crop Pests and Diseases
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4ef1d32e-3cdc-4be: Emanuel J. Lacy shows you some home remedies for common pests and diseases of fruit and vegetable crops. Whether you're a nervous amateur or a skilled farming expert, you're sure to learn something!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5ce3eb48-4fb0-4b2: Hey there, I'm Emanuel J. Lacy, and this is my garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e380bbe4-5754-49d: There's nothing more disheartening to a beginning farmer...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e9715519-9884-41a: ...  than seeing their early shoots succumb to disease or pests.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5f51986b-a4e7-41f: But don't worry! Here's a few home remedies you can use for common problems.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_31afbd65-ce98-481: Mildew is a white fungus that grows on leaves due to humidity and warmth.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_05902a3e-b7f4-4aa: It can be gotten rid of by spraying milk on the affected areas.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_225f4cb5-a5d6-488: And now for some moo-re tips. Hehe.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_91604c9f-0474-47c: At some point, your crops are going to be attacked by flies, but the cure is simple.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_3803df9e-dd55-4f1: Tobacco! Add cigarettes to your garden water sprayer, and apply it to your plants.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8e2aef63-eeac-4aa: Slugs will strip your greens to the bone. Don't let it happen!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_7bbe8d80-92ff-4f2: Place a container with a little bit of beer in it near the affected area.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ff72678b-cdac-481: The slugs will smell the beer, fall in, and drown.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bfe0a688-9cda-423: Reminds me of my college days. Hehe.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ffb502eb-214a-4e0: Got aphids? A spray of disinfectant mixed with water will get rid of 'em.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_fecbb4ec-0945-4fb: As for devil's water fungus... the cure is simple.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4adc559b-4265-496: VHS: Better Fishing With Jason Master
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9a1671e8-7158-4c4: Reel 'em in better than ever with Jason Master's fishing masterclass! From baits and rods, to tips and tricks, you'll catch everything from minnows to pikes with ease!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ec7dd489-2b32-42b: [img=music] Heck, I'm no good at fishin', don't know my rod from my line... [img=music]
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4c1edd02-5fb3-458: [img=music] I need someone to help me, I'm sick of all this tryin'... [img=music]
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_0b56335c-3d8e-45f: [img=music] Well bud, you're in the right place. You want to catch 'em faster... [img=music]
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_68a9da56-a5e6-4c6: [img=music] Try this here great video from expert Jason Master. [img=music]
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9c7f7d85-864a-442: Hey fisherfolks! I'm Jason Master, winner of the World Angling Cup, '83 through '92.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a77dd237-a561-4cd: Today I'm gonna give YOU some tips for catching everything from minnows to pikes.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4e4b41ab-a2af-43b: The first thing is a good rod.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c986dc2e-050e-44a: Ain't gonna catch much with a stick and a piece of string!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e19eb784-9676-4ac: Look for ripples or bubbles on the surface. That's where the fish are.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_15a42c26-38b9-48e: Third thing: bait. Use a lure if you can...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e62b4bb9-0e58-4f0: ... but you can also try a worm, an insect, or a little bait fish.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_09749620-37a0-452: Easiest way to get worms from the soil is at dawn after it's rained...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e7f19ddc-744c-484: ... with a trowel or hand fork.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_f30f1685-39cf-4dc: Or my brother Billy'll sell you a bucketful in Frankfort!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8cbe45ba-3b9c-448: Then cast your line. And wait. And wait...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_57e39b9c-b6d8-4e6: If you followed my tips, you'll soon get a bite!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_3269f70f-0eee-4c3: Reel 'em in as quick as you can without stressing your line to breaking point...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_890581ca-0196-4cc: Gosh-darn it, my arms need a rest. Have fun fishing!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_b4a4beaa-64c2-474: Petting zoo owner Tilly shows some of the cute animals she cares for every day.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_054b7530-8802-474: Hi, I'm Tilly, and today I'm treating you to a special tour of my petting zoo!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d91bd941-32f3-4b3: I feed Laura from a bottle.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1d91fbe0-92dd-482: Grown up boy animals can fight with each other so we keep them separate.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d9f11d3f-333d-42a: Here's the Gobbler family. They're turkeys!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_992318e1-f096-4e8: Have you ever had a turkey's egg? They're delicious!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_83f5116b-2884-4bb: Pinny is our baby deer. We found her in the forest.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c75ba851-f0a1-494: Some hunters had shot her mom.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_22efa6ac-6819-4be: Thankfully, Pinny can nearly look after herself now, can't you darling?
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_db03387e-4571-4e1: Thank you all for joining me today. Perhaps we'll see you again one day soon!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ae2d9265-69d8-45a: VHS: A Day on the Farm
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9471f3a8-d187-48c: Farmer John and his wife Hannah show you a typical day on their animal farm.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_b384fbc1-2547-471: Oh boy, Poppy the cow sure needs a-milking.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_38ca7a9c-7f36-415: Half a dozen eggs today. Hannah, warm the skillet!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_3728cf18-1884-45a: John, I'm gonna feed the pigs now!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_f999f5e7-1629-49c: That's for you, Bessie. And you, Arthur...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_6c66eebe-487e-44e: You don't need that wool for the summer, Norman. Let me help you.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_912a3093-0603-46e: <yawns> Another long day on the farm. Goodnight John.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_adc63e0b-f173-405: Learn your amps from your volts with the help of Ed Willis, winner of Southern Illinois Electrician of the Year three years running.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_290f9a34-c007-4f0: Hi, I'm Ed Willis, winner of Southern Illinois Electrician of the Year three years running.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5ab74162-939b-47a: Electricity is a powerful natural force, consisting of a flow of electrons, negatively charged particles,
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_00410808-fc09-45e: The rate of flow of electrical current is measured in amperes.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_92a51307-5810-4cb: Voltage is the electric difference between one charged point and another.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c61bb731-f37a-447: Electricity flows from a higher voltage point to a lower voltage point.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_0fa2d613-c0af-476: Ohms are the measurement of resistance. An electrical charge often has to be limited...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_39a66905-1a09-450: ... to ensure a circuit doesn't burn out.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a1230de7-2546-410: Here is a basic battery circuit illustrating these principles.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_0e7667be-58e0-40b: Hopefully, these basics will help you on your electrical journey.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a670df23-5d0e-449: Join Chief Hospital Corpsman Ivan Phillip Keaton of the USMC to learn the basics of how the military treats its wounded.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_718c7182-58c1-438: Hi. I'm Chief Hospital Corpsman Ivan Phillip Keaton. I'm a Green Side medic, assigned to the Marines.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_20aae55b-f938-41d: We lost some good men in the Gulf...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_55e9c6f0-a689-461: ... but we would have lost a lot more without our skilled medical corps.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_7cad8717-e8dc-494: Today we're going to walk you through some typical combat wounds.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bbf1c2b3-e8eb-41c: A lodged bullet must be extracted with tweezers.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5f6e68b2-6667-4d5: Then the wound must be sutured with a suture needle and thread.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_97ebc440-e0d1-4a4: Finally, put a clean bandage over the wound.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_91283d09-ed61-4f2: Painkillers will help manage the pain...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5b57f3b8-aa45-457: ... and antibiotics should be kept on hand in case of infection.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_179a21a8-118a-4af: Pieces of metal or glass shrapnel follow a similar procedure.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ac9b3cad-7bff-422: Remove the shrapnel, then either bandage the wound if it's not deep...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5cbf01e3-e99f-46f: ... or disinfect, suture and bandage if it is.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_75de44e9-f33e-4e6: Follow these steps and your men will live to fight another day.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bc21e1ed-f99b-4ae: Doctor Carol Susa of Rosewood Medical brings you some first aid tips for common injuries.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_fe0010c2-8cb6-4b9: Hello. I'm Doctor Carol Susa of Rosewood Medical.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9f76aa23-d52f-471: First aid is not as tricky as it first seems. Unless you're hemophobic, of course.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d57d2fdf-bae5-4e4: The first thing to do is assess the severity of a wound.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e95e7f38-5309-4e8: A bandage should stop the bleeding on a scratch or shallow wound...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_033fe82c-c42a-462: ...but deep cuts will require suturing at a hospital.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_df96f5f0-1a8f-492: Make sure the wound is kept clean, and the bandage is sterile.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_66142a5a-860a-4e5: Disinfectant or, in a pinch, alcohol, will stop infection setting in.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_21dc2f27-3700-4d7: Burns take a long time to heal, and the dressing must be kept...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_63812feb-d3af-475: ...very clean and changed as often as possible.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_31090446-4387-42e: Severe wounds must be treated by a doctor. Do not attempt self surgery!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5ef4af17-de3f-412: Fractured bones can be helped heal with splints.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9fdb149c-6ba7-4ca: Bleeding wounds to the neck or head are extremely serious...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_6bb436c1-739b-444: ...and it is imperative you dial 911 immediately should one occur.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1677d450-d555-4e5: This covers all the major injuries you or a loved one are likely to sustain.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4d1db334-80f6-477: And if something bad does happen to you, remember Rosewood Medical!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8aa2ce62-e48e-42d: Learn what to do in a medical emergency with the help of paramedic JG Narwhal.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_20a89632-4bc5-4ad: Hello there, I'm JG Narwhal, a paramedic from Louisville, Kentucky.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4a7dd8fc-5993-4cf: The best way to help any casualty is to dial 911, but you may need to help before the paramedics arrive.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_94f41100-88fb-464: D - Danger. Before treating a patient ensure there's no danger to you.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a2a20493-1307-404: R - Response. Does the patient respond to their name, or a tap on the shoulder?
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_674825a0-fa1c-4ee: A - Airway. Is the airway open? Tilt their head upwards if not.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_3df58c91-79c1-4aa: B - Breathing. Is the patient breathing? If not, you will have to perform CPR.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_b47fd19c-57dd-410: And finally C, Circulation. Is the patient bleeding?
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_fd132c42-ef16-480: If so, clean the wound with disinfectant, and cover with a bandage.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_971b76eb-7799-4df: Splinters or shrapnel can be removed with tweezers, unless deep in the skin.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1db1000c-eb71-41f: Bruising is a sign of internal bleeding, and should be treated at a hospital if serious.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_7eeae353-2f6b-4eb: If external bleeding is severe, apply pressure to the wound.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a6374c2a-e81e-448: If you've dialed 911, an ambulance should soon arrive to help you.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_199fc9cf-b9e7-451: You've done your part, so let the professionals take it from there.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5de52a43-19b4-4b6: Before metalworking, for hundreds of thousands of years, humans shaped stones into tools, weapons, and constructions. Dr. Jane Nightly explores the forgotten, ancient art of stone knapping.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c9e7dacd-4d8d-431: For hundreds of thousands of years, humans worked to shape stones to meet their needs.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e9710437-f8bb-456: Tools, weapons, religious idols... each shaped with the ingenuity of early man.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_813faa41-92f9-467: The two most common stones used in knapping were flint and chert.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_381e1654-4f2e-428: A chert stone was used as a hammer to shape the flint, or remove flakes from it.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1da43b13-3f48-486: Later, the chert was attached as a head to a wooden handle, as a simple hammer.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d61c1404-3931-404: Flint flakes could be fashioned into blades or points, and used as knives...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_115f878d-01dc-40c: The ancient Egyptians made bracelets and armlets from flint...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_bb10c4ee-a1a2-4ad: ... while the Mayans fashioned elaborate ceremonial objects from chert and obsidian.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_68da4b4a-3757-47f: Some of these items have lasted for up to two million years.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_3d22bdae-8e78-42c: We have to wonder how many of our modern tools will last as long.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_fb5343c4-4856-4fa: Blacksmith Edmund Jonson details the basics of metalworking, from finding the ore, to making the final product.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_01841e8f-7789-444: Welcome to my workshop. I'm Edmund Jonson, blacksmith.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ffcca2db-982f-422: All metal originates from the earth's crust.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_dc1e16af-406e-47c: Ore is mined, by hand or machine, and then processed and purified.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8b3c6e5c-3b7d-4bc: These days, blacksmiths create their work from commercially available ingots.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ef79a00d-7c7c-4ba: These ingots may be elemental, like iron or gold, or an alloy, like steel.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_87004378-ed1c-425: Furnaces come in many forms, but they all melt metal, usually using charcoal as fuel...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_071e00ea-fb70-4c6: ... which is then shaped into ingots or bars using a clay mold.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_13681dcd-3dc8-42b: The more intricate shaping and heating of the metal happens at the forge.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a78381b0-4f59-45f: With practice, you can make everything from a simple baking tray...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_de60cfc0-c517-4f2: Keep your nose to the grindstone and who knows what you can forge!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1edae24e-86e8-49b: Adefope Fencing is Virginia's number one metal fencing provider. In this limited edition video, Head Welder Mark Steier takes you behind the scenes to see some of the secrets of welding and metal construction.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_48913287-be32-4b8: Hello there. You might be wondering how we at Adefope's Fencing...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8e7598e4-125d-414: ...make our strong and stable metal fences.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_1ae83b2e-e77c-412: Come join me on a tour of our factory, and wonder no more!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4e9f2ce0-a46d-4b5: Our basic metal fence is created from a metal pipe...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_7eb41a5a-039f-47c: ...a small metal sheet, and three pieces of scrap metal.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5dd9e3ed-964c-4bd: Our skilled welders can turn these simple materials into something special.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_45fa0c4b-ea3b-4bd: Our most popular item, the pole fence, is made from three poles...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c6291e5c-c1bb-448: ...and the larger version is five poles along with two pieces of scrap metal.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_96ae24c3-a2b6-4e0: Our wired fence is nothing more than a roll of wire...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_12cf811e-c2be-482: ...plus scrap metal and two metal pipes.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_f8d1ffd6-7c2a-414: And our tall wire fence, made from three rolls of wire...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_28c04674-f2dc-464: ...three pipes and four pieces of scrap metal will let sunlight in...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_cb28f5f2-cbd1-4f3: ...while keeping foxes, wolves or feral pigs out of your garden.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_b8a6effc-e7bc-4bc: For a free consultation and a catalog from Adefope Fencing...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_2d3be6e2-71d5-49b: Want to start welding but don't know where to start? This handy video guide will give you all the basics you need to become a master.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_af97a48a-974f-41c: Hi there! I'm Charli, San Franciscan by birth, welder by trade.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_5ad26d63-3f7c-4bb: Welding is, simply, joining together two metals using heat.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d59ed795-d276-406: For everything but the most basic constructions, you're going to need welding rods.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_0a714b36-532e-404: And don't forget to wear your mask!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ab7f6df0-615c-43c: Hold the rods like so, where your two pieces meet. Then bring the flame down, moving it along...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_78738761-540f-426: ... until the rods melt and bind them.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_25edb20c-e8f3-4a3: That's the basic principle of all welding, from your living room shelf...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4c2174ac-9c99-48c: Yannah Hyerson has been guiding novice pottery students for almost forty years. Now, let her guide you in the art of clay shaping and pot making. The only thing you need - is the clay!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_ff5b977b-53e1-4e2: Welcome to my pottery class. I'm Yannah Hyerson.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_91fef801-c2d4-44a: To start, all you need is a pottery bench or wheel, and some clay.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c47057f8-1c65-443: Clay can be purchased at craft stores or even found in the ground if you're very lucky.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_004e5978-9614-4d3: Most pottery items require clay and water or sand.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8048dd7b-7cd0-4a1: It's best to start simple with bowls or mugs before advancing...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_434c4484-67e4-494: ... to more exacting items like clay bricks or tiles.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_843e2497-2537-4f5: The sculpted clay objects are then fired in a kiln to harden them.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8eaa1dc5-1816-4d9: And don't worry if your sculpt collapses, or your clay is too runny or thick.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_93b48a8b-cebe-462: It's all part of the learning process. Don't give up!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_02119190-b737-442: Learn all about sculpting and glazing clay with renowned expert Viktor Davenport.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a45f69ed-c415-4e3: Pottery is an ancient craft, and still a helpful one today.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_2190cadf-8cd6-498: The basic ingredients of all pottery are clay and sand or water.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e573f31b-91bd-439: Clay is shaped at a bench or wheel.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_4530ea49-791f-4f0: Glazing is an important step to turn basic pottery into something more ornate.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_68a60a37-05b2-494: Use a small brush to cover your shaped clay item with glaze.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_739794ce-df75-4a0: Now, when you fire it in your kiln, the pottery will be stronger, and waterproof.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_c6db2289-a28c-488: From bowls and cups, to smoking pipes and tiles, pottery is the art with a thousand uses.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_6280e1a7-8f99-402: Do you throw out your clothes as soon as they get a hole in them? This VHS will show you the basics of sewing and stitching so you can wear your favorites for longer.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_39c9b680-713e-434: Hi there, I'm Gerald Grant. I've worked as a tailor in Louisville for almost twenty years.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_a9b8d6bd-0cba-41c: Today I'm going to share some of my secrets to make your clothes last longer.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_b0f5296d-f07d-4ae: The basic tools of my trade are a needle, thread, a scissors, and scraps of extra materials.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_621b451d-03f5-492: Small holes can be stitched like so. Thread the needle...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_43c67679-9842-43c: ... then pull and push it through at small intervals.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_d1cdde00-e680-48c: Cut your thread at the end, and tie a knot in it.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_55f590dd-a5ab-431: For larger holes, you will need extra fabric to attach, but the principle is the same.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_e82bb4ed-cd11-4d9: Put the material in place and sew it securely.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_cc400841-8dd8-48e: With enough practice, you can even make things look as good as new!
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9fc64f2b-f6d6-47f: Denim and leather items are tougher to cut and stitch...
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_9a197257-f480-4d5: ... but with the right materials, it can be done.
values.Recorded_Media.json|RM_8d355623-d87e-497: And remember the old saying: a stitch in time saves nine!

values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_RuralLooted_tooltip: The chance that any rural building will already be looted when found.\nCheck the "Advanced" box below to use a custom number.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_MaximumDiminishedLo: The maximum loot that won't spawn when Days Until Maximum Diminished Loot is reached.\nCheck the "Advanced" box below to use an exact percentage.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_MaximumLootedBuildi: If a building has more than this amount of rooms it will not be looted.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_MuscleStrainFactor_: Functions as a multiplier when applying muscle strain from swinging weapons or carrying heavy loads.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_DiscomfortFactor_to: Functions as a multiplier when applying discomfort from worn items.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_WoundInfectionFacto: If greater than zero damage can be taken from serious wound infections.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_NoBlackClothes_tool: If true clothing with randomized tints will not be so dark to be virtually black.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmUseDamageCha: Replaces Chance-To-Hit mechanics with Chance-To-Damage calculations.  This mode prioritizes player aiming.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmNoiseMultipl: A multiplier for the distance at which zombies can hear gunshots.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmMoodleMultip: Multiplier for Moodle effects on hit chance. 0 disables Moodle penalty.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmJamMultiplie: Multiplier for firearm jamming chance. 0 disables jamming.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmWeatherMulti: Multiplier for the effects of weather (wind, rain and fog) on hit chance. 0 disables weather effect.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FirearmHeadGearEffe: Enable to have headgear like welding masks affect hit chance
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_BasementSpawnFreque: How frequently basements spawn at random locations.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_EasyClimbing_toolti: Disables the failure chances when climbing sheet ropes or over walls.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_SpottedLogic_toolti: Activates the new advanced stealth mechanics, which allows you to hide from zombies behind cars, takes traits and weather into account, and much more.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_MaximumFireFuelHour: The maximum hours of fuel that can be placed in a campfire, wood stove etc.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FenceThumpersRequir: How many zombies it takes to damage a tall fence.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FenceDamageMultipli: How quickly zombies damage tall fences.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_ClayLakeChance_tool: Chance to turn a dirt floor into a clay floor. Applies to lakes.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_ClayRiverChance_too: Chance to turn a dirt floor into a clay floor. Applies to rivers.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_GeneratorVerticalPo: How many levels both above and below a generator it can provide with electricity.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_DayNightCycle_toolt: Whether the time of day changes naturally, or it's always day/night.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_ClimateCycle_toolti: Whether weather changes or remains at a single state.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_FogCycle_tooltip: Whether fog occurs naturally, never occurs, or is always present.
values.Sandbox.json|Sandbox_UniqueHomeVHS_toolt: If true only one instance of an individual Home VHS tape will normally spawn.

values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_walking: To move your virtual legs, use %1%2%3%4. This is called walking. <LINE> You can also tap %5 to Run, or %6 to Sprint. <LINE> Careful now - Running or Sprinting is loud and can attract the dead.
To move your virtual legs, use %1. This is called walking. <LINE> You can also tap %2 to Run, or %3 to Sprint. <LINE> Careful now - Running or Sprinting is loud and can attract the dead.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_climbin: You can climb over tall fences by tapping %1 when standing next to them. <LINE> Watch your Encumbrance - carrying a heavy load can make it difficult to climb!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_vaultin: You can hop fences by tapping %1. You will also vault them automatically when running - but that doesn't work so well with walls. <LINE> Mind your step - clumsy folk may trip and fall!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_aiming_: Hold down %1 and move your mouse to look around and aim. <LINE> Remember to check behind you - though there's probably nothing there!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_strafin: Move while aiming to Strafe. <LINE> Strafing is a way to sneak while looking around, though you will move at a slower pace.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_sneak_f: Press %1 to sneak and keep low. To hide more effectively, sneak beside short fences and vehicles. <LINE> Crouching will not stop the undead from seeing or hearing you if you get too close!  <LINE> Be mindful it uses more Endurance than simply walking.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_backpac: You can drag and drop items from your inventory into backpacks, containers, and inventory slots. <LINE> The left inventory window shows everything you are carrying. The right window shows the contents of any nearby containers or items on the ground. <LINE> Use %1 to select multiple items, or %2 to select individual items.

You can drag and drop items from your inventory into backpacks, containers, and inventory slots. <LINE> The left inventory window shows everything you are carrying. The right window shows the contents of any nearby containers or items on the ground.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_double_: Double click an item to do a contextual action. <LINE> It will equip clothes and weapons, read a book, or grab an item from a container.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_weight_: How much you can carry is limited by your Strength and Moodles. <LINE> Items in equipped bags weigh less than those in your main inventory. <LINE> Different bags have different capacities and weight reductions.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_right_c: Many items have advanced options which can be found using %1. <LINE> Try it on televisions, radios, generators, and even a toilet bowl if you're desperate!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_doors_d: Press %1 or %2 to open and close doors. Doors keep zombies out, and can be barricaded for extra strength. <LINE> Just don't depend on it holding forever!
Press %1 to open and close doors. Doors keep zombies out, and can be barricaded for extra strength. <LINE> Just don't depend on it holding forever!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_windows: Tap %1 once beside a window to open or close it. Hold %2 to climb through. <LINE> You can force a locked window open quicker by tapping %1, but sometimes its lock will break. You can still smash it open - but be mindful of broken glass!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_curtain: Curtains and sheets can be attached to windows to block their view. <LINE> Open and close them using %1 and %2.
Curtains and sheets can be attached to windows to block their view. <LINE> Open and close them using %1 and select "Open Curtains".
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_lights_: %1 powered lights or light switches, to turn them on and off. <LINE> Remember, more light means it's easier for the undead to see you too!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_map_des: Use %1 or click %2 on the left to open your map and see where you are. The map can be filled in through exploration and by finding Maps or Flyers to reveal locations. <LINE> You can make markings on your map using a pen or pencil. <LINE> Don't get lost!

Use %1 and select %2 to open your map and see where you are.  The map can be filled in through exploration and by finding Maps or Flyers to reveal locations. <LINE> You can make markings on your map using a pen or pencil. <LINE> Don't get lost!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_flashli: Equipped flashlights can be turned on or off with %1. <LINE> All flashlights need battery power to work, and make you more visible in the dark. <LINE> Flashlights don't scare away the monsters.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_televis: Televisions and radios let you tune into news, music, and more. Some let you watch VHS tapes or CDs. <LINE> Certain shows will give you skill points or new recipes. <LINE> Just don't fall in love with the Woodcraft guy.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_bad_gas: With appropriate skills and recipes, you can connect a generator to your house to provide power. <LINE> Never use a generator indoors - the fumes will damage you!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_equip_p: Equip a weapon by using %1 on it, then selecting "Equip Primary". <LINE> You can use anything from a katana to a keytar - though results may differ!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_melee_a: Aim an equipped melee weapon by holding %1, and use %2 to strike. <LINE> You strike towards the isometric cursor. <LINE> If a zombie is too close for a weapon's range, you will shove them instead.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_shove_d: Press %1 to shove a zombie away. You can also press %2 to stomp a downed zombie. <LINE> Using your feet will spare your weapon's condition. <LINE> Make sure to aim for the head!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_stealth: Feeling brave? Equip a knife and sneak close behind an enemy. Aim, wait for your hand to raise - then strike! Silent but deadly.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_shootin: Aim an equipped gun with %1, and use %2 to fire. The smaller the crosshair, the more accurate your shot will be. <LINE> Your chance of hitting anything is influenced by your Skills, Moodles, light levels, and more. <LINE> Try not to shoot yourself in the foot.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_reload_: Use %1 to reload using unboxed ammo. Ammo can be unboxed using the %2 menu. Some guns require Magazines to work. Hold %3 for more advanced reloading options.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_zombie_: If the undead surround you, they can drag you down and kill you instantly! <LINE> Attacks from the rear are especially dangerous. Sadly, there is no way to make friends with a zombie.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_shoutin: Press %1 to shout and attract nearby zombies. Do this while crouching and you will whisper. <LINE> You can use some items to make louder noises like whistles, harmonicas and more. <LINE> Despite reports to the contrary, shouting, unfortunately, does not cure the Knox Virus.

Press %1 and select %2 to shout and attract nearby zombies. Do this while crouching and you will whisper. <LINE> You can use some items to make louder noises like whistles, harmonicas and more. <LINE> Despite reports to the contrary, shouting, unfortunately, does not cure the Knox Virus.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_hotbar_: Use the hotbar for quicker access to your weapons. Use %1 to attach a weapon to a hotbar slot, then press the corresponding number or %2 to equip it. <LINE> Worn belts and holsters give you more hotbar slots to use.
Use the hotbar for quicker access to your weapons. Use %1 to attach a weapon to a hotbar slot, then press %2 to equip it. <LINE> Worn belts and holsters give you more hotbar slots to use.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_fence_d: Zombies will stumble when climbing over fences or through windows <LINE> You can use this to your advantage - if they don't lunge and get you first!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_open_ca: Food in cans or jars can be opened using the Crafting menu or the %1 menu on it. <LINE> Cans need a Can Opener or a Blade to open.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_food_pr: Use the Crafting menu or %1 on cooking containers like Bowls, Roasting Pans, or Saucepans to prepare food recipes. <LINE> Some may need the container to be filled with water first. <LINE> You can learn new recipes from magazines and TV shows.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_cooking: Put your food item into an oven, microwave, BBQ or other appliances, then turn it on using the button on the bottom to start cooking your food. <LINE> Don't forget to turn your oven off - unless you have a fire extinguisher to hand!

Put your food item into an oven, microwave, BBQ or other appliances, then turn it by using %1 to start cooking your food. <LINE> Don't forget to turn your oven off - unless you have a fire extinguisher to hand!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_liquid_: Use %1 to fill a Liquid Container eg. a Water Bottle, and see its options. <LINE> Use the Transfer Liquid menu for more advanced options. <LINE> Open topped containers can collect rainwater. Note that Tainted water is bad for your tummy! %2
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_treat_w: Tainted water (usually from a river or collected rain) is unsafe for drinking. <LINE> Boil or use Purification Tablets to make it safe.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_moodles: The Moodles on the right represent your character's needs. <LINE> Green is good %1, red is bad %2. <LINE> If you see this one, %3, you don't need to worry about anything anymore.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_eating_: Double click or use %1 on a food or drink item to consume it. <LINE> By default, clean water in your main inventory will be automatically consumed to keep your thirst at bay. <LINE> Remember to eat a balanced diet or you may gain or lose weight!

Use %1 on a food or drink item to consume it. <LINE> By default, clean water in your main inventory will be automatically consumed to keep your thirst at bay. <LINE> Remember to eat a balanced diet or you may gain or lose weight!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_first_a: Use %1 or click %2 on the left to open your health menu, and %3 to apply remedies to your injuries %4. <LINE> Many items of clothing can be ripped to get a Rag to use as a bandage. <LINE> To avoid infections use a disinfectant on the bandage or directly on your wound.

Use %1 to open your health menu %2, navigate the tabs using %3/%4, and %5 to apply remedies to your injuries %6. <LINE> Many items of clothing can be ripped to get a Rag to use as a bandage. <LINE> To avoid infections use a disinfectant on the bandage or directly on your wound.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_rest_de: Don't let tiredness %1 and exhaustion %2 sneak up on you! It will severely limit your awareness and capabilities. <LINE> Rest in a chair to catch your breath, and sleep in a comfy bed for better results. <LINE> Sleeping Tablets or Painkillers may help - but best not to mix them with alcohol.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_exercis: Running or moving heavy loads will make you stronger overtime. <LINE> But you can also gain Strength and Fitness using exercises on the Health menu. Be mindful of muscle strains or the next day you'll be in dire pain. <LINE> Even in the apocalypse, you can be beach body ready!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_skill_b: Some books will give you a Skill Multiplier to level up a skill faster. <LINE> You can also learn Crafting Recipes from Magazines, VHS tapes, or some other special items. <LINE> Leveling up skills will sometimes unlock new Recipes too.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_bad_sme: The apocalypse is filled with nasty smells. %1 <LINE> Don't hang around in areas with lots of dead bodies for too long, or you may get sick. Move away, bury or burn them, or wear a mask!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_craftin: Press %1 or click %2 on the left to open the Crafting menu. <LINE> Use %3-%4 on an item to search how to produce it, and on an output item to search where it can be used.
Press %1 and select %2 to open the Crafting menu.
Some Crafting Recipes can be created almost anywhere using the Crafting Menu, with the proper materials and tools. Some simple Recipes can be crafted directly from your inventory using %1.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_craft_o: Some Crafting Recipes need a hard surface like a table or a workstation - or even a boulder! - to be performed. <LINE> Stand beside one of these surfaces and open the Crafting menu %1 to see them.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_sheet_r: Use %1 on a window to attach an Escape Rope with a nail. You need just a single nail and a hammer, but one rope for every floor to the ground (eg. two ropes from the second floor). <LINE> We haven't taught the zombies how to climb (yet), but they can still tear down your rope.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_build_m: Click %1 on the left to access the Build Menu. <LINE> This allows you, with the correct materials, to build static world objects and furniture like Fences, Walls, or Workstations. <LINE> Go and build yourself a post-apocalyptic mansion!

Press %1 and select %2 to access the Build Menu. This allows you, with the correct materials, to build static world objects like Fences, Walls, or Workstations. <LINE> Go and build yourself a post-apocalyptic mansion!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_barrica: Use the Build Menu %1 or use %2 on a window or door to Barricade it. You'll need a Plank, Nails, and a Hammer for a basic wood Barricade. <LINE> Barricading gives door and windows more Health.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_build_w: Wood or Metal walls require a Wallframe to be built first. <LINE> You can then fill the frame with walls, door frames or window frames. <LINE> A door will first need a door frame, while a window will need...  you guessed it, a window frame!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_craftin: Building workstations will let you create more advanced recipes. <LINE> There are many to build, from Furnaces to Churn Buckets and Drying Racks, some with unique functions!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_start_v: If you're in a vehicle and have its key, use %1 to start the engine. Use %2%3%4%5 to drive and steer. Drive cautiously! Engine noise will attract zombies. <LINE> A vehicle's dashboard will show you important information, and allow you to unlock the doors or trunk.

If you're in a vehicle and have its key, use %1 to start the engine. Use %2 to drive and steer. Drive cautiously! Engine noise will attract zombies. <LINE> A vehicle's dashboard will show you important information.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_vehicle: Press %1 in or near a vehicle to see its options. <LINE> This will allow you to do things like add Gas, lock doors, or smash the car's windows.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_gas_ref: Without Gas, a vehicle can't move! Use the %1 menu to add Gas, if you have a container with Gas in your inventory or are beside a gas pump. <LINE> You can fill any Liquid Container with Gas from a powered pump. <LINE> Remember to check your fuel gauge to see which side the gas cap is on.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_mechani: Press %1 by your vehicle's hood, or use the %2 menu and select %3, to see your vehicle's condition. A vehicle in poor condition may need repairs. <LINE> The Mechanic skill makes this easier! And no nasty repair bills afterwards.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_trailer: Use the %1 menu to attach %2 or detach trailers %3 close to the back of your vehicle. <LINE> Trailers add extra storage space or allow you to transport animals, but also affect the vehicle's handling.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_vehicle: Vehicle trunks can store a large amount of items - or a corpse or two. <LINE> Glove compartments and even seats can also be used as storage space.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_seasons: It's not just zombies that are a threat in Knox Country. <LINE> Rain, snow, fog, and other adverse weather conditions can freeze or wet you, and lower visibility, especially in winter. Don't catch cold!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_tempera: Appropriate clothing will keep your temperature regulated. Too high or low temperatures will negatively affect you. <LINE> Some clothing offers protection from more than just the elements, and can even be reinforced with Tailoring!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_foragin: Click the spyglass icon %1 on the left to open the Investigate Area menu. <LINE> This window shows details on your surroundings. Click "Enable Search Mode" to begin Foraging. You may find Berries, Mushrooms, Animal Tracks - and lots more. <LINE> The menu will even show you the position of the sun, and phase of the moon!

Pressing %1 and selecting the spyglass icon %2 to open the Investigate Area menu. <LINE> This window shows details on your surroundings. Press %3 to begin Foraging. You may find Berries, Mushrooms, Animal Tracks - and lots more. <LINE>  The menu will even show you the position of the sun, and phase of the moon!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_mining_: You can use a pickaxe to remove small-to-medium rocks or other obstacles in the world. <LINE> Aim at the rock and press %1 to break it down into usable pieces. <LINE> Do not hit your pet rock by accident.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_open_se: Seeds have to be removed from their Packets before planting. <LINE> You can do so by using %1 on a seed packet, or using the Crafting menu.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_dig_fur: Seeds can only be planted in outdoor furrows, at ground level. Use a Trowel, Shovel or, if you're desperate, your hands to dig a furrow in soil or grass. <LINE> To do so use %1 and select Dig Furrows under Gardening. <LINE> You might also find some wiggly worms - and you can call them Jim if you want to!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_sow_see: Plant seeds by using %1 on a dug furrow. <LINE> You can then use %1 or %2 on your plant to check its information panel. <LINE> Be mindful of the season and needs of your crops.
Plant seeds by using %1 on a dug furrow. <LINE> You can then use %1 on your plant to check its information panel. <LINE> Be mindful of the season and needs of your crops.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_harvest: Done all the hard work? It's time to harvest your crops! Use the "Harvest option" by pressing %1 on the plant. <LINE> A high Agriculture skill means more crops will be harvested.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_animal_: Click %1 on the left to create Zones for your animals. <LINE> Calm animals will never leave their Zone, even if it's unfenced, as long as they have water and no zombies are around... <LINE> A Zone's info panel shows its food, water, and all animals within the zone.

Press %1 and select %2 to create Zones for your animals. <LINE> Calm animals will never leave their Zone, even if it's unfenced, as long as they have water and no zombies are around... <LINE>  A Zone's info panel shows its food, water, and all animals within the zone.
Press %1 near an animal or %2 on it to find options for your it, including their Info. <LINE> Skilled Animal Carers will see more information on their animals.

Animals need food and water to survive, which can be added to troughs or dropped in their Zone. <LINE> Animals will breed on their own. Just make sure your animals' bloodlines remain a tree, and not a circle!

Being around zombies, noise, or shooting nearby will create Stress for animals, and affect their health. <LINE> Building trust is important with your animals. Time, love, and plenty of treats will help. <LINE> Don't stress the bull or you'll get the horns!
You can put a rope on an animal by pressing %1 near it to move them around easily. <LINE> You can also attach them to a tree or a pole. <LINE> Be aware they can break the rope if too stressed.

Chickens and turkeys need a hutch to sleep safely at night. You can use %1 to open the hutch menu and watch over them. <LINE> Be sure to close the door at night, and open it in the morning to not stress your birds. <LINE> You must have a rooster with your hen to fertilize eggs.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_butcher: Animals can be killed by combat or by using the %1 menu near them. <LINE> While big animals require a Knife, smaller ones can be killed by hand! Just like Grandma used to do. <LINE> Animals butchered on a Butcher Hook will provide Leather and more Meat.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_petting: Petting an animal will reduce its Stress - and yours! The Stress reduction is limited to once per day. <LINE> You can even befriend rats. The apocalypse is a lonely place after all!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_fishing: Ripples indicate fishable water. <LINE> Use %1 to open the Fishing Panel. This shows fish you've caught, along with information affecting the fish. <LINE> Skilled Fishers see more information.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_add_bai: Add bait to your Fishing Rod using %1 on it to increase your chance of catching a fish. <LINE> Different bait will attract different types of fish.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_cast_an: With your Rod equipped, use %1 and %2 to cast. <LINE> Watch the tension meter to see when you have a bite, then reel in with %3. <LINE> Reeling too fast will snap your line.

With your Rod equipped, use %1 and %2 to cast. <LINE> Watch the tension meter to see when you have a bite, turn counter-clockwise %3 to reel in and clockwise to release tension. <LINE> Reeling too fast will snap your line.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_trappin: Place Traps in the world to catch small animals. Use %1 on a Trap in your inventory to place it, then use the %2 menu on it to add Bait. <LINE> Baited Traps only catch animals if you're far enough away for some time. <LINE> Traps can catch living animals like Rabbits or Raccoons, but some animals, like Birds, will always be killed by Traps.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_burn_co: Too many corpses in one area causes Sickness. Hold %1 beside a corpse to drag it. <LINE> Corpses can be buried in graves or burned with gasoline and a fire source. <LINE> The latter is better for your back!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_cleanin: The apocalypse can be a messy place. Use %1 with a cleaning fluid (eg. Bleach, Gasoline) and a cleaning tool (eg. a Sponge) to see cleaning options.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_clean_s: Keep your face and body clean with Water. A dirty body makes wound infections more likely! Soap will do a better job. <LINE> Seriously, wash yourself once in a while, we can smell you through the screen!
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_laundry: Eventually, your clothes will be covered with dirt and/or blood. These make wound infections (but not zombie infection) more likely, so keep them clean with Soap and Water. <LINE> You can even use a washing machine if you're too lazy to do it by hand.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_activat: Click on %1 to turn PvP Safety on or off. <LINE> When PvP Safety is off, a skull will appear beside your username. <LINE> Two players with PvP Safety on cannot attack each other, but a player with PvP Safety off can attack anyone.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_faction: Click on %1, then Create Faction to create an invite-only group, with private chat. <LINE> PvP can be disabled against fellow members, and members show on each other's Maps. <LINE> Note: faction members don't necessarily share Safehouses, which is done using the Safehouse menu.
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_multipl: Press %1 to type in chat. Your chat can be preceded by commands: /all (global chat, won't attract zombies), /say or /s (local chat), /whisper or /w followed by username (private message), <LINE> /yell or /y (shout), /safehouse or /sh (safehouse members), /faction or /f (faction members), <LINE> /admin or /a (admin chat), /r or /radio (message using equipped radio).
values.SurvivalGuide.json|SurvivalGuide_medical: Use %1 on a player and select the option to perform a Medical Check. <LINE> Here you can provide aid to other players - or check for a dreaded bite mark.

values.UI.json|UI_optionscreen_heart_volume_tt:
The two major sounds heard in the normal heart sound like "lub dub".
The "lub" is the first heart sound, commonly termed S1, and is caused by turbulence caused by the closure of mitral and tricuspid valves at the start of systole.
The second sound, "dub" or S2, is caused by the closure of aortic and pulmonic valves, marking the end of systole.
